items.definition:
a fragrant herb used in cooking
I added some fresh oregano to the pasta sauce.

a room with facilities for washing, typically a public toilet
Excuse me, where is the nearest washroom?

yellow wild flower
Children often hold a buttercup under their chin to see if they like butter.

holder for a candle
She placed the candle in the silver candlestick.

a person employed to stand at the entrance of a building
The doorman greeted us as we entered the hotel.

a bucket
The child carried a small pail to the sandbox.

a three-wheeled vehicle
The toddler learned to ride his new tricycle in the park.

a large, bowl-shaped frying pan
She stir-fried the vegetables in a hot wok.

a piece of furniture with shelves for books
She arranged her books neatly on the new bookcase.

a crescent-shaped pastry
She enjoyed a warm croissant with her coffee.

A cloth or brush for removing dust.
She used a feather duster to clean the shelves.

a small, spicy root vegetable
She added sliced radishes to her salad.

a board with a smooth, dark surface for writing on with chalk
The teacher wrote the lesson on the chalkboard.

baby carriage
She pushed the baby in the pram through the park.

the bank of a river
We enjoyed a picnic on the riverbank.

a dark red root vegetable
She added some roasted beetroot to her salad.

A chain for holding keys
He keeps his house keys on a small keychain.

a dish of ice cream with fruit, nuts, syrup, etc.
I ordered a chocolate fudge sundae for dessert.

pain in a tooth or teeth
I have a terrible toothache and need to see a dentist.

a kidney-shaped edible nut
I like to snack on cashews.

a female lion
The lioness protected her cubs fiercely.

a single drop of rain
A single raindrop fell on my nose.

academic tasks or studies done by a student
I need to finish my schoolwork before I can play.

a yellow flower with a trumpet-shaped center
Daffodils are one of the first flowers to bloom in spring, bringing a splash of yellow.

a Spanish title or form of address for a man, corresponding to Mr. or sir
"Excuse me, Señor," she said, trying to get his attention.

a container for carrying a packed lunch
She packed her sandwich in her lunchbox.

the action of teaching a person or animal a particular skill or type of behavior
She is undergoing intensive training for the marathon.

an electric light
The lightbulb in the lamp needs to be replaced.

a stepmother
My stepmom is very kind to me.

a cup from which tea is drunk
She poured the tea into a delicate teacup.

a band worn around the arm
The captain wore a special armband to identify his role.

a meal or party at which food is cooked outdoors on a grill
We're having a barbeque in the backyard this Saturday.

a type of flower, typically with a ruffled appearance
She wore a red carnation pinned to her lapel.

An area for dancing.
The dancefloor was packed with people.

A machine used for cutting grass.
My dad spent all morning fixing the lawnmower.

a sequence of numbers or characters used to gain access
Please enter your passcode to unlock the phone.

a photographic copy of a document
I need to make a photocopy of this document.

a substance or preparation for killing germs
Always carry hand sanitizer when you're out.

a loose two-piece suit worn for exercise or casual wear
He put on his tracksuit before going for a run.

a watch worn on the wrist
He checked the time on his new wristwatch.

a cloth spread over a table
She put a clean tablecloth on the dining table.

a loose robe, typically made of terrycloth, worn before and after bathing
He put on his soft bathrobe after his shower.

grandfather (informal)
My granddad always tells the best stories.

a waterproof coat.
Don't forget your raincoat; it's going to rain.

A machine that makes copies of documents.
The office copier is out of toner again.

a person who jogs, especially regularly
The park was full of joggers enjoying the morning air.

a small, round beetle with a red or orange back with black spots
A ladybug landed on my hand in the garden.

Small box for matches
He lit the candle with a match from the matchbox.

a young duck
A mother duck led her ducklings to the pond.

the governing body of a state
The government announced new policies to boost the economy.

the act of removing hair with a razor; a thin slice or strip
He finished his morning shaving quickly.

a handle for opening a door
She turned the doorknob and entered the room.

short for chocolate
Do you want a choc biscuit?

short for chocolate
The kids love choco milk.

a salad of shredded raw cabbage, usually with a mayonnaise or vinaigrette dressing
We had coleslaw with our barbecue.

a pole on which a flag is flown
The flag was raised to the top of the flagpole.

a small ball of chewing gum
He put a quarter into the machine and got a red gumball.

a dome-shaped Eskimo house, typically built from blocks of solid snow
The children built a small igloo in the backyard after the heavy snowfall.

a type of lettuce
I prefer romaine lettuce in my Caesar salad.

an outdoor area next to a school
The children played soccer in the schoolyard.

a musical instrument
The child shook the tambourine to the rhythm of the music.

A sauce made from cooked apples
She served pork chops with a side of applesauce.

a pedestrian crossing
Always look both ways before stepping into the crosswalk.

A dish made from beaten eggs cooked in a pan.
He cooked a cheese omelet for breakfast.
